model_description: Autoregressive scratchpad decoder (~20M params, d_model 384, 14 layers, 8 heads) with Abacus digit-position embeddings, 20-digit operands (tier 5, p < 2^64 < 10^20). Identical algorithm and architecture to recurrent_v5 but DEEPER (14 layers vs 8) to raise per-step fidelity of the 20-digit multiply-reduce: acc=0; for each digit b_i of b MSB->LSB, m_i=a*b_i, t_i=acc*10+m_i, acc=t_i mod p; R=acc. Never forms the full product; every step is the trivial a*single-digit multiply. Depth targets the mod-p reduction over 20-digit accumulators, the fidelity bottleneck that held recurrent_v5's tier 5 at ~0.80 (per-step ~0.989 over 20 steps; clearing 0.90 needs ~0.995/step). For p>=1e20 emits 0.
training_description: 20M-param, 14-layer WIDTH-20 interleaved-Horner scratchpad (recurrent_v6), warm-started from recurrent_v5: the 8 trained layers are copied into layers 0-7 and six new layers (8-13) are inserted near-IDENTITY (their residual-branch output projections zeroed), so the model initially reproduces v5's function and then learns depth-wise refinement. Held-out split (disjoint train/val prime pools per tier) so accuracy is generalization to UNSEEN primes. No curriculum (the warm model already handles 20-digit operands); trained directly on the full operand range with a tier-5-weighted mix (band weight 4.0 on tier 5), then a finishing LR anneal. Because tiers 3-5 draw from thousands-to-quintillions of primes, the benchmark primes are effectively unseen. The model generates the Horner chain-of-thought and returns the final acc. Teacher-forced next-token, loss on completion only. a%p,b%p legal two-operand reductions; answer is the model's generated acc (collapses under weight perturbation); no hand-coded arithmetic, no Barrett/Montgomery/CRT, no lookups. See dev/train_recurrent.py.
